name: Massachusetts
overview: Massachusetts cities and towns, not counties, collect property tax. If a tax on land is not paid within fourteen days after demand, the town's collector can take the land for the town, creating a tax title, a limited ownership held by the town or a third party that buys or is assigned it; the account then moves from the collector to the treasurer. The owner can redeem by paying the tax title with simple interest of 16% a year, or 8% for tax titles entered on or after November 1, 2024. After 6 or 12 months the holder can bring a foreclosure case in the Land Court, and once it is foreclosed the town may keep the property or sell it, listing it with a broker within 180 days; former owners can claim the excess equity from a sale.

counties.office: City of Springfield Collector-Treasurer (Office of the City Treasurer)
counties.address: City Hall, Room 112, 36 Court Street, Springfield, MA 01103
counties.next_sale_note: No auction after 2026-10-27 posted. The latest was the City's first Real Estate Auction of 2026, held Tuesday, February 3, 2026 at Springfield City Hall (past).
counties.how_to_bid: Auctions are held in person at Springfield City Hall. Under the terms of sale for the February 2026 auction, each property (acquired by the City through tax foreclosure) required a $5,000 deposit by certified check, verified before the auction started, and carried a 5% buyer's premium; the balance was due at closing. The prior owner or anyone acting for them, and anyone who owes the City money, cannot buy.

counties.office: Town of Abington Treasurer (Tax Title Custodian)
counties.next_sale_note: No auction after 2026-10-28 posted. The latest notice read was for a tax possession auction on Wednesday, March 12, 2025 (past).
counties.how_to_bid: Based on the Town's notice for its March 12, 2025 tax possession auction: the Treasurer, as Tax Title Custodian, sold town-held tax possession parcels at a public auction held at 78 Linda Street, Abington (one of the parcels), with open house and preregistration starting 30 minutes before. Deposits were set per parcel ($20,000 and $10,000 at that sale), a 7% buyer's premium applied, and the balance was due within 30 days by bank cashier's or certified check unless otherwise announced. Parcels were sold as is, the buyer also paid pro-rata taxes and recording charges, and the Custodian could reject any bid or withdraw a parcel. Terms for any next auction are not posted.
